hypothesis: If Darwin's inference holds, the numeric age of the latter part of the Secondary (Mesozoic) period, the late Chalk or Late Cretaceous, in the International Chronostratigraphic Chart is at least about 300 million years before present.
pass_criterion: The ICS chart gives the top of the Cretaceous, the end of the Chalk-depositing interval and the Cretaceous/Paleogene boundary, an age of at least 300 Ma, or at least 270 Ma if the 10% rounding tolerance of 'roughly 300' is applied to the lower bound. Confirmation also needs the base of the Upper Cretaceous (Cenomanian) to be at least 270 Ma.
fail_criterion: The ICS chart gives the Cretaceous/Paleogene boundary an age below 270 Ma, or the Upper Cretaceous interval (Cenomanian base to Maastrichtian top) lies entirely below 270 Ma. This is expected: the chart gives about 66.0 Ma for the K/Pg boundary and about 100.5 Ma for the base of the Upper Cretaceous, so the claim is refuted by a factor of about 4.5 or more.
interpretation: Darwin's 'latter part of the Secondary period' is mapped to the Late Cretaceous, the age of the Chalk. His 'years elapsed since' is mapped to the numeric age in Ma of the top of the Chalk-bearing Cretaceous interval. Darwin's own arithmetic of 1 inch per century on a 500-foot cliff, scaled up to the Weald's width, is not tested here. The test compares his total of about 300 Myr with the modern radiometrically and astronomically calibrated timescale. Darwin treated the figure as a minimum ('far more than'), so a chart age below 300 Ma refutes it. Modern work also treats the Weald's denudation as largely Cenozoic uplift and erosion, not steady cliff retreat, but only the elapsed-time quantity is tested.

dataset.name: International Chronostratigraphic Chart
dataset.why_it_fits: The chart is the standard public reference for numeric boundary ages. Its downloadable PDF and the machine-readable versions linked from the page give the ages of the Cretaceous/Paleogene boundary, the Maastrichtian, Campanian and Cenomanian stages, and the Upper Cretaceous series. These are the fields used: the stage and series names and their boundary ages in Ma. They decide directly whether about 300 Myr, or more, has passed since the late Chalk.
